summary.one_liner: Ren'Py is a visual novel engine, and this repository is its source code, with development branch guidance, build instructions, and contribution rules.
summary.what_it_does: The README is mainly a contributor and build guide rather than a feature list. It explains the branch layout (fix, master, work/, history/) and which branch takes fixes versus features. It describes how to get a nightly build and run ./after_checkout.sh, or compile the Cython and C modules yourself with uv sync and ./run.sh. It covers building the Sphinx documentation from docstrings tagged with :doc:, :name:, and :args: fields. It also states the project's policy on AI and efficiency tools and the MIT license for contributions.
use_cases: compile Ren'Py C and Cython modules
how_to_run: Download a nightly build and unpack it, then change into the repository
Run ./after_checkout.sh to set up the nightly modules
Alternatively, install system dependencies (libsdl2, ffmpeg libraries, python3-dev and others) listed for Ubuntu/Debian
Run uv sync to create a virtual environment and install dependencies
Run ./run.sh to compile extension modules and start Ren'Py
Install Sphinx and run ./build.sh inside the sphinx directory to build docs
notable: Branch model separates fix (maintenance) from master (feature development), with work/ branches for pull requests
Docstring-driven documentation generation using :doc:, :name:, and :args: tags
Build scripts for nightly builds (after_checkout.sh) or compiling modules from source (run.sh)
Explicit policy that changes must be human-reviewed; unreviewed agent or vibe-coded changes are not accepted
Allows machine translation of system messages when no human translator is available
caveats: Setup.py does not support cross-compiling; the README points to a separate renpy-build system for other platforms
Scripts assume a POSIX-like platform; Windows needs an environment like MSYS
Compiling modules requires many system dependencies, and SDL_image 2.6 or greater is needed
